name: Clover-35B-A3B-Preview
context_scaling: Native 131,072 from config.json max_position_embeddings; no rope_scaling block. The card states prompt plus generated response must fit inside 128K together. rope_parameters: partial_rotary_factor 0.25, rope_theta 10000000 - the partial rotary rotates 64 of 256 head dims and is a NoPE trick, it does not shrink the cache.
attention_variant: Block-diffusion MoE on the Qwen3.6 hybrid GDN backbone: 30 of 40 layers are gated linear attention (linear_attention), 10 are full_attention (full_attention_interval 4), GQA 16 heads / 2 KV heads, head_dim 256. DiffuSpace adds bidirectional GDN parameters - right-convolution weights and softmax controls - so tokens attend within a noisy block while the resolved prefix stays causal.

benchmarks.name: SWE-bench Verified
benchmarks.config: Vendor run, printed in the Chinese launch blog prose verbatim ('SWE-bench Verified 达到 73.6') and read independently off the blog's agentic-benchmarks.jpg figure; both agreed. Harness not printed. Competitor cell on Clover's own figure for Qwen3.6-35B-A3B is 65.8, while Qwen's own card records 73.4 for this test - see notes, the +7.8 headline is DiffuSpace's re-run, the +0.2 is the same-test vendor-vs-vendor delta.

benchmarks.name: Terminal-Bench 2.1
benchmarks.config: Vendor run, printed in blog prose and read off agentic-benchmarks.jpg. Harness not printed. Same figure: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B 43.1, and the blog claims a win over LLaDA2.2-flash, Mercury 2.5, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B and Qwen3.5-35B-A3B. Catalog's nearest same-test entry is xing4-0-29b-a4b Terminal-Bench 2.1 57.5 at 4B active, which beats this row.

benchmarks.name: Tau3-Bench Overall
benchmarks.config: Figure row label is 'τ³ Overall' - the aggregate over the τ³ domain set, not a single domain. Blog prose repeats 65.3. Same figure: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B 43.4. Catalog's Tau3-Bench best at ≤4B active is xing4-0-29b-a4b 64.63, which this edges by 0.67 - a margin inside cross-harness noise, not a clean upset.

benchmarks.name: BFCL-v4
benchmarks.config: Vendor run, read off agentic-benchmarks.jpg; blog prose repeats BFCL-v4 67.9. Same figure: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B 63.4. Loses to the catalog's spark-x2-6-4b BFCL-V4 71.8 (4.11B dense).

benchmarks.name: SWE-bench Pro
benchmarks.config: Figure row label 'SWE-Pro'. Vendor run. Same figure: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B 42.7, but Qwen's own card records SWE-bench Pro 49.5, so this row flips sign depending on which Qwen column you trust. Loses to spark-x2-6-4b SWE-bench Pro 54.3.

benchmarks.name: Terminal-Hard
benchmarks.config: Figure row 'Terminal-Hard'. Vendor run, no harness printed. Same figure: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B 31.8. No catalog record carries this test, so it is recorded for completeness and compared to nothing.

benchmarks.name: GPQA Diamond
benchmarks.config: Blog prose and general-benchmarks.jpg agree: 83.8. Same figure: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B 83.3. LOSES to Qwen's own card value of 86.0 (row labelled 'GPQA' there, Diamond not confirmed) - so the claimed edge over its base does not survive against Qwen's own published number, only against DiffuSpace's re-run.

benchmarks.name: MMLU-Pro
benchmarks.config: Blog prose 84.8 and figure 84.8 agree. Same figure: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B 84.7. LOSES to Qwen's own card 85.2. A statistical tie either way.

benchmarks.name: ZebraLogic
benchmarks.config: Blog prose 95.8, figure 95.8. Same figure: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B 78.6 - the largest single gap on the general figure (+17.2). Catalog's best ZebraLogic is olmo-3-7b 32.9, on a different scale/prompt, so no cross-record claim is made.

benchmarks.name: AA-LCR
benchmarks.config: Blog prose 72.0, figure 72.0. Same figure: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B 66.0. LOSES to the catalog's sage-a1-5 AA-LCR 81.0 (3.0B active) - so long-context recall is not a class win.

benchmarks.name: AIME 2026 (avg@8)
benchmarks.config: Figure row 'AIME 2026 (avg@8)'. Vendor run. Same figure: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B 90.4 - a LOSS of 7.1 to its own base, and the biggest regression the vendor's own figure shows. Recorded because the card prints it.

benchmarks.name: MATH-500
benchmarks.config: Figure row. Ties Qwen3.6-35B-A3B at 96.2 on the same figure. The blog also quotes a MATH-500 throughput figure (101.8 tok/s at INT4 on one RTX 5070 Ti) - that is a speed measurement, not a score, and is not recorded as a benchmark row.

benchmarks.name: SciCode
benchmarks.config: Figure row. Same figure: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B 31.3 - a small LOSS. Loses badly to spark-x2-6-4b SciCode 36.8 and gemma-4-12b 39.8 in the catalog.

benchmarks.name: IFBench
benchmarks.config: Figure row. Same figure: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B 61.3 (+11.0). Loses to spark-x2-6-4b IFBench 75.8.

benchmarks.name: Humanity's Last Exam (text-only)
benchmarks.config: Figure row 'HLE text-only'. Same figure: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B 21.2 - a LOSS of 8.4, the second real regression on the vendor's own figure.

notes:
ADDED 2026-10-29 from the HF trendingScore feed (rank 6 at read time, 105 downloads, 114 likes, repo created 2026-10-24 - a launch-week card). DiffuSpace is a Dream-7B-lineage team (HKU NLP alumni) and this is their first model.

WHY IT IS A 'diffusion' + derivative_kind 'other', NOT A FINETUNE: the YAML tag says base_model Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, but the tensor set and the config are not the base's. Clover adds bidirectional GDN parameters (right-convolution weights, softmax controls), a block-diffusion head with denoising_config {algorithm: low_confidence, threshold: 0.95}, block_size 32, moe_block_coreset_enabled true with top_p 0.9, and denoising generation parameters (dllm_length_penalty 10.0, dllm_think_end_bias 10.0). So it is a re-architected derivative, which is why architecture is 'diffusion' rather than 'moe' and derivative_kind is 'other' rather than 'finetune'. Its 40-layer / 30-GDN + 10-full-attention backbone, 256 routed experts, top-8 routing, 1 shared expert, hidden 2048, head_dim 256 are inherited unchanged.

PARAM DERIVATION: params_b 34.661 = safetensors.total 34,661,350,848 from api/models?blobs=true. The card says 35B total / ~3B active; active_params_b 3.0 is taken from the vendor claim (top-8 of 256 routed experts plus 1 shared expert), not recomputed - the config carries no expert intermediate width for the shared path that would let the estimate be tightened beyond the vendor's own figure. flops_per_token_active = 2 x 3.0e9 = 6.0e9, which is the AR per-token cost; for a diffusion LM this is per denoising step, not per emitted token (see KV below).

KV DERIVATION: kv_cache_bytes_per_token = 20,480 = 10 full_attention layers x 2 KV heads x head_dim 256 x 2 (K and V) x 2 B. The 30 GDN layers hold a recurrent state instead of a per-token cache. Identical to the Qwen3.6-35B-A3B base record (20480), which is the expected result for an inherited backbone. IMPORTANT DIFFUSION CAVEAT: this is the cost of caching the *resolved prefix*, and the prefix does grow per block, so unlike llada-8b it is NOT a zero-cache model. Each 32-token block is denoised bidirectionally in parallel and re-forwarded until resolved (threshold 0.95, at least one position per step), so compute per emitted token is (denoising steps for that block) x (a forward pass over prefix + block), not one decode step. That makes it prefill-shaped on the weight stream - the 34.7 GB BF16 is re-read per step - which is exactly why the team ships self-speculative decoding in SGLang and llama.cpp rather than plain batching. A full 131,072-token context costs 131,072 x 20,480 B = 2.68 GB of growing KV.

SPEED CLAIMS (vendor, not recorded as benchmark rows): 680 tok/s aggregate at BF16 batch 1 on one NVIDIA GB300 on internal agent data; 515 tok/s on one H200 in agent tasks versus 365 tok/s for the 'DFlash2' Qwen of the same size; 101.8 tok/s at INT4 on one RTX 5070 Ti with 16 GB, versus 48.5 tok/s for comparable MiniCPM/Qwen (DEFAULT serving config, no scaffold stated). The blog is explicit that the HF PyTorch path and the SGLang kernels produce different text, and recommends SGLang for evaluation.

CONTESTS (this is why status is contested, not verified): the whole benchmark set is vendor-run and published only as blog JPEGs plus prose. On the four tests where the catalog holds the base's own vendor number, Clover's figure of its own base disagrees materially with the base's card: SWE-bench Verified Qwen column 65.8 here vs 73.4 on Qwen's card; SWE-bench Pro 42.7 here vs 49.5 there; GPQA Diamond 83.3 here vs 86.0 there; MMLU-Pro 84.7 here vs 85.2 there. So DiffuSpace re-ran Qwen under their own scaffold, and every 'beats its base' claim in this record is only true against that re-run. Against the base's published numbers the honest reading is: ZebraLogic +17.2 and IFBench +11.0 are the only two large wins; SWE-bench Verified +0.2, MMLU-Pro -0.4, GPQA Diamond -2.2, and it LOSES outright on AIME 2026 (-7.1), HLE text-only (-8.4), SciCode (-0.4). We do not resolve this by picking a column - both numbers are kept.

CLASS CONTEXT: the interesting fact is not a benchmark edge but that this is the first open 35B-A3B diffusion LM and the vendor's claim is that at this scale diffusion stops losing to AR of the same shape. Two independent catalog models still beat it on individual tests (xing4-0-29b-a4b Terminal-Bench 2.1 57.5 and Tau3 64.63; sage-a1-5 AA-LCR 81.0; spark-x2-6-4b BFCL-v4 71.8, SWE-bench Pro 54.3, IFBench 75.8), so it is not a size-class upset on the tests this catalog tracks - it is a new architecture worth running.

HARDWARE GATE: active 3.0B <= 40 and 34.661 x 0.5 GiB = 17.3 GiB <= 128, so it passes the offload gate - but only via expert offload, and the diffusion re-read per denoising step means the routed-expert stream is paid once per step, not once per token. On this user's low-VRAM box that is materially worse than an AR 3B-active MoE, and the vendor's own edge demo needed 16 GB for an INT4 build. That trade is the reason it is recorded and not recommended.

GAPS: no GGUF from the vendor at read time (llama.cpp support is claimed in the blog and a third-party q4 file was not verified); the block-diffusion code is custom_code (auto_map CloverMoeConfig/CloverMoeModel/CloverMoeModelLM) so plain Transformers loading needs trust_remote_code with transformers 5.19.0; no harness is printed for any row.
